slides.heading: Tuberculosis (TB)
slides.subtitle: The world's deadliest infectious disease and a major public health problem — Koch's disease.

slides.heading: Overview
bullets: AKA Koch's disease / galloping consumption / phthisis.
Badly nourished, neglected, fatigued individuals are more prone; susceptibility highest in children <3 yrs.
Causative agents: Mycobacterium tuberculae, M. africanum, M. bovis.
Incubation period: 2–10 weeks; transmission: droplet/airborne (thrives in absence of sunlight).
Signs/symptoms: cough (>2 weeks), anorexia, chest pain.

slides.heading: Diagnostics
bullets: Gene Xpert — confirmatory.
Sputum smear microscopy — alternative (BHW collects, medtech analyzes); contraindicated in hemoptysis (refer if massive).
PPD/Mantoux/Tuberculin — test for exposure, read at 48–72 h: general population >10 mm, immunocompromised >5 mm.
Chest X-ray — most common.

slides.heading: Management & DOTS
bullets: Check liver function; high-caloric diet; avoid physiotherapy.
TB DOTS (Directly Observed Treatment, Short-course) — taken before meals.
Control: BCG vaccine, exposure to direct sunlight, reusable utensils.
Categories: New (<1 month treated), Retreatment (>1 month), Relapse, Loss to follow-up, Treatment after failure.

slides.heading: National TB Control Program
bullets: Vision: a country where TB is no longer a public health problem.
Mission: ensure TB DOTS services are available to communities.
Targets: cure ≥85% of sputum-smear-positive patients; detect ≥70% of estimated new cases.

slides.heading: Key Takeaways
bullets: Cough >2 weeks → screen for TB; Gene Xpert confirms.
RIPES side effects: Rifampicin (orange), Isoniazid (neuritis → B6), Pyrazinamide (uric acid), Ethambutol (eyes), Streptomycin (ears).
Mantoux positive: >10 mm general, >5 mm immunocompromised.
DOTS taken before meals; check liver function during therapy.
